Sorrowsong University #1

Nightshade

Autumn Woods, Ruxandra Tudor (Translator)

4.08
100,276 ratings19,803 reviews
Rate this book
Mister. Crimă. Răzbunare. Bine ai venit la Universitatea Sorrowsong!

El este dușmanul ei. Ea este lumea lui.
El va arde lumea pentru ea... dar ea o va arde din temelii pe a lui.

Ophelia Winters vrea răzbunare.

Izolată în Munții Scoției, Universitatea Sorrowsong primește de obicei doar studenți din cele mai puternice și corupte familii. Ophelia nu are ce căuta acolo, dar o bursă neașteptată îi oferă ocazia perfectă de a investiga moartea „accidentală” a părinților ei în apropierea universității.

Din păcate, începe ancheta cu stângul când intră într-un conflict cu misteriosul Alex Corbeau-Green, fiul principalului ei suspect. Din punctul de vedere al Opheliei, el este doar o versiune mai tânără a tatălui său miliardar. Un monstru sub o mască frumoasă.

În ultimii patru ani, singurătatea a fost singura prietenă de încredere a Opheliei. Dar când un hărțuitor necunoscut începe să o urmărească și să o tortureze, își dă seama că s-ar putea să nu poată supraviețui singură la Sorrowsong.

Alex devine aliatul ei neașteptat – și alibiul pentru crimă. Iar pe măsură ce ea începe să se îndrăgostească de inima plină de compasiune ascunsă sub înfățișarea de bărbat dur, flacăra răzbunării amenință să se stingă pentru prima oară.

Oare chiar va putea să distrugă tot ce a cunoscut el vreodată?

Sexy, plină de suspans și întunecată, cu o poveste de dragoste enemies-to-lovers, Nightshade este lectura dark academia perfectă pentru cititorii care au adorat seria Maxton Hall.

About the author

Autumn Woods

4 books4,036 followers
Autumn Woods is the Sunday Times and USA Today bestselling author of the Sorrowsong University series. She writes gothic and gloomy settings with love stories that’ll tear you apart just to put you back together again. Her books have been translated into twenty languages.

Outside of writing, she is a book illustrator and an aerospace engineer, and you’ll often find her climbing, painting, baking, or walking the British countryside with Mr Woods and their dog.

“You make me finally understand what people mean when they say life isn’t long enough.”

No words just Alex Corbeau Green. Aka my new husband. Aka the most pathetic, sad boy, obsessed, tortured yearner on the planet. I am so done. I have a problem. I can’t remember the last time a fictional man had me this down bad. I actually can’t handle it.

This book was EVERYTHINGGGGGGG THEY ARE EVERYTHING!!! I need book two more than I need air to breathe the ending actually made me cry WHAT?! The banter, the spooky gothic university setting, the murder mystery/stalker plot, the suspense, the romance, the pain, the mental health rep, Ophelia made me feel so seen and heard. They literally flirt via email and through crosswords. Bye. This man tattooed, glasses wearing, intellectual, witty, flirty, man who draws her and washes his hair and is like a father to his 6 sisters?! No his backstory is actually making my chest ache. PROTECT HIM AT ALL COSTS I well as they drag me away to the padded room.

I cannot.

“I’ve built my walls too high.” “They’re worth the climb.” “They aren’t.” We stop on the mansion steps, his tone soft. “They are. For me, they are.”

“If you end up being the death of me, Winters, I couldn’t ask for a better end.”

“Then I’ll love you with the same intensity that you hate me. I’ll hold on to you just as hard as you push me away. I’ll fix you like you’re fixing me. I’ll always be here, Ophelia, I’ll sit at the bottom of valleys and stand on the top of mountains with you.”

“Forget dying for her. I’d live for her. I feel like I could overcome all the darkness inside if only it meant I’d get a life in her company in return.”

“Ophelia is my deadly nightshade. She’s bad for me. I know what she’ll do to me, but she’s too beautiful. Too enticing. She’s too deep in my bloodstream already, painful and ecstatic all at once.”

“Ophelia feels like finding another human after months in the desert. A light permeating the thick black cloud. When my wayward mind wanders, it staggers back home to her.”

As much as I had fun with it, it was far from perfect imo. I definitely see the appeal but it's probably one of those cases where my high expectations let me down. With the way everyone hyped it up, I was expecting a lot more than what I got.

The dark academia vibes were really good and immersive. The writing was okayish I suppose. I loved the way it started but it lost its rhythm in the middle. There was always something missing, not sure what but it just didn't feel like it was clicking. Parts of it felt a bit juvenile in the way it was written.

The characters were alright. Imo Alex carried the book, he really is a charming guy. I loved his sarcastic quips and wit. But also how appreciated how upfront he can be. He is the kind of mmc who immediately captures your attention. Ophelia on the other hand was a mess. She was fierce one moment, then completely weak the next moment. I just think there was more potential to her than what we saw.

The chemistry between the two though is pretty good. I enjoyed the romance and slow build. The push and pull on Ophelia's end got me annoyed at one point though. The banter between her and Alex was chef's kiss. The spice could have been a bit more steamy imo but I guess the author was going for a tasteful approach, which is probably just me nitpicking atp. Sorry 🫣 At least I'm self aware 😭.

The ending was really fun to get into. I won't deny that. The way it ended had me shook and baffled at the audacity to not immediately give us the next book 👁👄👁 But I'm looking forward to reading the next one and hope that it's a bit mature in it's writing.

Thanks to sweet Meg for reading it with me. BR are always fun with you 🥰

“Then I’ll love you with the same intensity that you hate me. I’ll hold on to you just as hard as you push me away. I’ll fix you like you’re fixing me. I’ll always be here, Ophelia, I’ll sit at the bottom of valleys and stand on the top of mountains with you. We’re too good not to work.”

How good was this?!?

I didn't get the chance to read much this week, but oh my days when I picked this book up- I could not stop. It was so damn addicting. The writing was definitely something I vibed with because it had me in a flow. There were some things that I struggled with- not enough to ruin my experience but enough for me to notice. I did like how atmospheric it was for me. It gave me this vivid image that I just loved. Also, I have no idea why, but this book made me so damn nostalgic (might be cuz I was blasting "ribs" on repeat, but it took me back to 2022 😭 and I loved it for that alone)

“I’ve built my walls too high.”
“They’re worth the climb.”

Ophelia, Nah because as soon as I saw that she was a redhead- I was on the floor. Litr me:

okay but actually she had me in a chokehold. Anyways besides that, she was a troubled character, carrying such heavy grief with her and trying to figure out her life, with everything including her feelings working overtime to be against her. It felt good to see her try and fail and then try again to navigate her way through. The snarkiness>>> 🫦 like guys how hot was that 🫣 Her solving crosswords even at the most intense moments was so 😭😭

“Ophelia is my deadly nightshade. She’s bad for me. I know what she’ll do to me, but she’s too beautiful. Too enticing. She’s too deep in my bloodstream already, painful and ecstatic all at once.”

Moving on to Alex, I GET THE HYPE. It was actually weird because would I categorize him as a broody bad boy? 🫳🫴 but he had those elements. He was actually respectful tho, which I liked. He might seem a bit intimidating from the outside, but he was very gentle, esp when you get to read his perspective. Reading the first chapter from his pov was so fun 😭 I also loved how unbelievably down bad this man was and everything that he did lowk felt effortless. It was like all the things were coming to him naturally 😭

“Fine, I want this. I want you. I can’t escape you, Alex. You’re like the sun. I turn away, I look down, but I can still see you reflected in everything at my feet. If I draw the curtains, you slip through the cracks. I can’t fall for the moon instead because it’s you that illuminates it. None of that changes the fact that we just won’t work. You’re not the problem here. It’s me, and things out of my control.”

The romance, was easily the best part about this book. Now, this made all the other things that I found lacking irrelevant, because the way the whole book was built around it, and esp with the way it was written 😮‍💨 the banter first of all?? Amazing. What makes a book super enjoyable for me is the THE. DAMN. BANTER. It was so beautifully delivered here. Their love actually felt like love. The chemistry?? INSANEEE. The tension? BURNING THROUGH THE PAGESS. Not to mention how both of them would shamelessly flirt. It was spicy, not in the sense that there were a lot of sex scenes but rather the situations, and the proximity, and how all of that was explored 🪭 oh my daysssss some of the best romance I have read in monthsss.

“One down. Seven letters. First letter O. I’ve had a long day, and I want her for dinner.” Holy fuck.” (best way to use crosswords)

Okay, moving on to the slight problems-
Plot the plot was okay at best. I liked the mysterious aspect regarding her parents' death, but truly if the romance wasn't there, I would've given up on it. The stalker's side quest was nice too, but with time it also became eh until the end, which was its peak imo Slight spoilersI don't understand when a character finds out who is after them while they are in front of them- why can't they act nonchalant and get out of it and then do smthing about it. ugh smh.

I also kinda wanted more from the side character only because they had a lot of potential but ig there is book 2 for it.

Overall, it was an amazing read!!

⤷ mini spoiler-free review!! ⋆౨ৎ˚⟡˖ ࣪

ˏˋ°•*⁀➷ my thoughts
i’m starting to think i’m actually the problem because somehow i always end up being the odd one out when it comes to fantasy books—i didn’t love this one and honestly, i haven’t loved any i’ve read so far this year 😭

don’t get me wrong, this book wasn’t all that bad. i loved the dark academia setting and vibes, and the mystery paired with the fast pacing kept me engaged throughout.

what fell flat for me was the romance. it feels like the enemies to lovers trope has been reduced to characters who “hate” each other while secretly lusting after one another nowadays, and this book leaned heavily into that. ophelia and alex’s dynamic often felt more like childish bickering than actual tension. they barely knew each other, yet for some reason they were completely obsessed with one another, with their relationship revolving almost entirely around physical attraction and sexual tension rather than emotional connection. on top of that, ophelia kept straying from her plan because of her growing feelings for alex, and the constant mention of how she shouldn’t like him but she does became tiring.

there were also times when i had to reread sentences just to understand what was going on, which occasionally pulled me out of the story.

ˏˋ°•*⁀➷ overall
while i didn’t love this book as much as most did, i still enjoyed it and would recommend it if you’re in the mood for a dark, atmospheric read this fall.

────────── ⋆⋅end⋅⋆ ──────────

I fear I ate this up 💅

🚨WARNING🚨 There’s a high chance you might find this predictable and cliché. Honestly, for most of it, I did too! And yet, somehow, Woods managed to keep me hooked. I couldn’t put this down. I think it’s one of those guilty pleasure reads where you know exactly where it’s going, but you’re still having the best time along the way. That said, there were definitely a few twists I didn’t see coming, and I really enjoyed myself!

“Oh… am I actually enjoying this?” That was my exact thought as I got deeper into the book. It starts off very been-there-done-that. Ophelia is the mysterious, gloomy girl, and of course, she meets Alex, the hot, rich, too-cool-for-you guy. Oh, and of course the elite school filled with insanely wealthy kids and their over-the-top connections. Yeah, yeah, I thought I knew where this was going. But then, a certain part of the plot grabbed my attention. Suddenly, there was mystery. And wait… was that angst I was feeling?! Oh, okay, well, now I have to know what happens. Some things did end up feeling a little too convenient, but I’m so glad I stuck with it because things got crazy by the end with some of those reveals.

I genuinely enjoyed all the characters. They were exactly the type you’d expect in a book like this, but that didn’t make them any less fun. Of course, I loved my main characters, and the more I got to know them, the more I liked them. They’re complicated in their own beautifully messy ways, thrown into situations they never saw coming. The romance? Yeah, I was into it. But I’ll admit I might have enjoyed their chemistry before they got together just a little more… but only because I’m a tiny bit toxic. Just a smidge.

The pacing was great, and the book even left me with a pretty cool cliffhanger—the kind that has me itching for the next one!

What to Expect:
➼ Hate to Love
➼ Forced Proximity
➼ Grumpy x Grumpy
➼ Murder Mystery
➼ Slow Burn
➼ He Falls First
➼ Romantic Suspense
➼ Cliffhanger
➼ Dark Academia/University Setting
➼ Duet Narration
➼ Dual First Person POV

That ending!! 💔 I need book 2 immediately!

Over 12,000 majority positive ratings before it was even traditionally published? When a book has this much hype, nine times out of ten I’m left disappointed, but I ate this one up! The overall tone of the book felt very romantic to me. The academic setting, the rainy weather, the star crossed feel of their relationship, etc. I kind of think of romance books like a recipe, a little of this trope, sprinkle in this genre or that, add in a little atmosphere, etc., and all I can say is that this author got the recipe exactly right. 🙌🏻

Hate to love is always a good place to start, but the reason for that hate needs to be justified but still forgivable for it to work and Autumn wrote those details perfectly. The book has a bit of a Mafia undertone that the MMC is distant from but still connected to. I loved that this was included but that the author still managed to write him as a very good and caring man with his own complex motivations for staying connected to the family business. The FMC has her own secrets and reasons to keep the MMC at arm’s length that added to the romantic suspense between them, and the tension was so good! She fought her growing feelings for him, but the plot continually threw them together in ways that were unavoidable and made the forced proximity make sense. The MMC was also just so gone for her in the best way. The more I think about it, He Falls First really might be the best trope out there and the author incorporated it so well here! His grumpy personality made his fixation with her that much sweeter, especially once we get to see his softer side when he goes above and beyond to care for her and his family. He’s actually perfect. 🥰

As far as the setting goes, I think anyone who’s been to college romanticizes an academic setting. Heck, just watching Gilmore Girls might be enough to romanticize it. That feeling of walking across the quad on an autumn day is already such a tangible feeling, but bringing that feeling to a Scottish Castle?! 👨🏻‍🍳💋 The atmosphere in this one can’t be beat!

I think this would make an excellent screen adaptation! I really hope we get one someday!! I genuinely won’t be happy until book two is in my hands! I need an HEA for Alex & Ophelia!

—— ✿ 3.5 stars

❛❛And God above, I’m sick of feeling sad, sick of not knowing how not to feel sad.❜❜

This was so fun! Admittedly I think my expectations may have been a bit too high given the hype, but for the most part I had a great time!

I told myself this review would be a short one but um I kind of got carried away. Whoops. Sorry?

꒰ ROMANCE ꒱
The romance progression felt inconsistent. There was a lot of push and pull between Alex and Ophelia, great back and forth from the first chapter, and then all of a sudden just push with no pull (he refers to her as the “ginger girl” and doesn’t notice when she’s left the room?), and then BAM a massive gigantuous pull. Their chemistry was all over the place. However, at about the 50% mark you kind of get past this weird rushed stage and I felt much more grounded in the story, and Alex… okay I get the hype now. I get it I get it I get it.

꒰ ALEX ꒱
Alex should be a professional juggler with how much life crap he takes on, poor guy with his thunder rugby thighs has the weight of the world on his shoulders. He’s patient, offering Ophelia reassurance whenever she needs it (yeah okay bare minimum but whatever Alex does is hot okay?) and is patient with her fear to commit to him even if it kills him. Don’t get it twisted, that doesn’t stop him from trying to convince her otherwise though, oh hell no. The quotes from this man??? Phewie.

“I like looking after you. It makes me feel better.”

Why is he so freaking sexy, it pisses me off.

꒰ OPHELIA ꒱
Speaking of fear of commitment and giving your trust wholly to someone, Ophelia was the echo to my soul. Her character is kind of all over the place, yet still in some ways relatable (although I’m so bad at crosswords I think she would have a meltdown). She’s just so sad, the embodiment of melancholy. She overthinks and lacks optimism - understandably after losing everyone she ever loved.

“Don’t break my heart. It’s fragile.” ☹️

But Ophelia also has a burning desire for revenge, and has this amazing ability at channeling her anger into snark towards Alex lol. She’s a paradox, albeit a messy and sometimes frustrating one.

꒰ MYSTERY & SETTING ꒱
The mystery plot was probably the most consistent out of everything. It was thrilling, tense, kept me on the edge of my seat even if it was predictable. And the setting was immaculate, all doom and gloom, just how I like it.

꒰ ENDING ꒱
However the ending had steam coming out my ears. Everything I thought would happen, but didn’t want to happen, happened. Thinking about the cliffhanger still makes me mad, I’m sorry 😭. Please give me the next book and please please please don’t drag things out 🙏🏻.

꒰ OVERALL ꒱
I’ve felt conflicted on how to fairly rate this as my expectations were sky high. Inconsistency was a running theme, and the ending had me so frustrated (I still can’t tell if this is a good or bad thing because I do need the second instalment like yesterday). But I genuinely really enjoyed a big chunk of this book, and found it hard to put down at many points.

And Alex Alex Alex… 🦵 More of his quotes as a thank you for your time:

“He didn’t deserve it.” “The date?” “That dress.”

“In a world full of complicated, Ophelia, my feelings for you are extremely simple”

“What’s stopping you?” “It’s complicated.” “Doesn’t matter. I’ll find it and I’ll fix it for you.”

“I’ve built my walls too high.” “They’re worth the climb.” “They aren’t.” We stop on the mansion steps, his tone soft. “They are. For me, they are.

“You make me finally understand what people mean when they say life isn’t long enough.”

“Then I’ll love you with the same intensity that you hate me. I’ll hold on to you just as hard as you push me away. I’ll fix you like you’re fixing me.“

Okay sorry I’ll stop now.

P.S. thank you Salma my buddy read queen for reading this with me. We’d wanted to read this together for ages but put it off until closer to the second book’s release. I now regret not waiting even longer 😭.

══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══╡ Overview: ╞══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══

⁀જ➣꒰ ⋮ ρℓσт.꒱

That book was not bad, but not great either—I enjoyed most of it. Maybe I went in with too high expectations, but I was a little let down by it. I expected way more than that. I see it has a lot of potential to be greater. Sometimes I felt bored due to the very long chapters.

The mystery plot was very intriguing, and I enjoyed it very much. This book was marketed as an enemies-to-lovers, and I didn’t see that at all. They just “hate” each other for a while, and then the lusting starts to happen. I was happy to be right about the plot twist, but I didn’t like the fact that it was so predictable. The cliffhanger was predictable, as well.

⁀જ➣꒰⋮ 𝕽𝖔𝖒𝖆𝖓𝖈𝖊.꒱

The back and forth with Ophelia quite bothered me. I loved seeing them in Chapter One, and then the chemistry felt lacklustre for me until the 50% mark. I started loving the romance between them after that, but at the same time, I felt like I needed more tension between them. The romance was a bit rushed. Also, I went into this book thinking it was spicy…and it wasn’t t at all. I was a little disappointed by that, to be honest. I don’t understand the need for “spicy” scenes if they’re not going to be detailed. (Oops, sorry, not sorry)

⁀જ➣꒰⋮ ᭙𝕣ⅈ𝕥ⅈꪀᧁ.꒱

The writing started out fine, but it just got worse later on. It was way too descriptive and felt like it lacked consistency.

══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══╡ Characters: ╞══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══

જ⁀➴ Ophelia: I’m so sorry to say this, but she has the personality of a cardboard. She was so, so bland and boring. I did not love her at all. I resonated with her backstory and need for revenge. But her feelings were all over the place; it was exhausting to read the same thing over and over again. I did relate to her in certain ways, but I didn't vibe with her personality.

જ⁀➴ Alex: He carried the entire book on his back, in my opinion. I adored him and even more so as the book went on. I hated the fact that he carries the weight of the world on his shoulders. Like, give the poor man a break for once. He is very charming, and I loved how he yearned and cared for Ophelia. I absolutely loved how he took care of his mom and his sisters. This man deserves more hype; he is so perfect. He is so husband material.

── .✦ 𝓕𝓲𝓷𝓪𝓵 𝓣𝓱𝓸𝓾𝓰𝓱𝓽𝓼: Overall, it was enjoyable, but it’s overhyped.
